label: 3-5 steps after a sequence-initial w
explanation: Fires in sequences whose first original token is w, at steps 3-5 (3 to 5 steps after that w), whatever the current input token is. first_tok==w covers 95% of activation mass (23.6x lift). The strongest activations are at t=4 (around 1.0 of max), then t=3 and t=5 (about 0.5-0.7). At t=5 it fires on an original token but not when t=5 is the <DEL> step (L=5); at t=3/4 it also fires on the <DEL> step. Activations are nearly zero at t<=2, at t>=6, and in the copy phase. Weak low-quartile activations happen when w is the second token (and similar lag), or with other first tokens. The current input token barely modulates it.

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says activations peak at t=4 (about 1.0 of max) and are weaker at t=3. On dev, t=3 and t=4 have almost the same number of active steps (21,841 vs 21,826), but t=3 carries more of the activation mass (0.518 vs 0.426). So t=3 is the stronger step on average. The t=4 values near 1.0 come almost entirely from sequences that start 'w w' (every top-12 example begins 'w w'). In ordinary w-first sequences, t=3 and t=4 are similar at about 0.3-0.6 (e.g. 'w 2 e [1:0.45] [p:0.43]', 'w i s [t:0.45] [h:0.39]', 'w x 3 [e:0.53] [k:0.33]').

The t=5 part of the predicate is weak. On test, first_tok==w & orig_idx==5 has precision 0.585 and mass recall 0.050, and it accounts for most of the 4,865 false positives (every one shown is at step 5). It is a fading tail, not a reliable firing step. By contrast, t=3 has precision 0.999 and t=4 has precision 0.956.
The <DEL> claims hold: first_tok==w at t=5 on the <DEL> step has precision 0.049, and at t=3 on the <DEL> step it has precision 0.97.

Recall is 0.75. The missed activations (21% of active steps, about 4.8% of the mass) are low-magnitude and spread over many first tokens and steps 2-5. The only consistent part is w as the second token at t=4, and it has precision 0.37. Adding it lowers F1 from 0.815 to 0.804, so it is not worth including. I found no systematic class of high-magnitude misses.
The copy-phase, t<=2 and t>=6 claims check out: 36 active steps in the copy phase, none at t<=1, and 69 at t=6 on dev.
The core label and predicate hold up, and none of the alternatives I tried scored better (test F1 0.815). The rejection is only because the explanation's t=4 peak claim is false.
skeptic.revised_label: 3-5 steps after a sequence-initial w (strongest and most reliable at t=3-4, weaker tail at t=5; peaks near max when the sequence starts 'w w')
